theorems.statement: If orbits a and b are co-component at state S, they remain co-component in every legal descendant. Hence if an R2 fires with both sq and tq inside an already-merged component, same_component holds automatically; if either lies outside it, same_component is NOT implied.
theorems.ground: incidence_components rebuilds from scratch unioning ('q',orbit)<->('h',hexagon_id(port)) per set orbit_masks phase bit; orbit_masks is add-only (extend line 245, no clearing operation exists); a union-find whose edge set only grows can only coarsen

theorems.statement: Any argument closing a family by proving same_component unreachable cannot apply once the relevant pair is already merged; for those pairs the condition is permanently true. MERGED_BY_R is exactly the class where hypothesis D3 of the generic T4 template fails at R1 -- the template's own dropped-hypothesis counterexample, realized.
H==0 is automatic on live paths (all RR-admissible joints have weight<=3, dH=max(w-3,0)=0), and kind==R forces new_orbit==False so tq is drawn from the finite already-open orbit set.

the natural coarsening that would prove it is unsound: quotienting by the component partition fails because new_orbit=(om[q]==0) distinguishes unopened from opened while a singleton-component partition does not, so identical partitions can admit different joint kinds (Z3 vs R), changing r_count and hence Target A
